subject: Intermittent egress stalls after route consolidation — OrbitBridge
messages:
From: NetOps <netops@orbitbridge.com>
To: logan.wright@redwood.com
Cc: sre@orbitbridge.com
Date: 2027-06-07T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Re: (no subject) — abrupt egress stalls after consolidation

Hi Logan,

We pushed the route consolidation into the east-west peering yesterday evening (changed two /24 next-hops to the new aggregator). Since the change we've seen intermittent egress stalls from our app fleet to several third-party APIs — flows open but packets stop for 30-90s, then resume. The timing aligns with ARP/adj flaps reported on our leafs immediately after the route sync.

Attached a pcap from one affected host (edge-trace-20270607.pcap) and a route delta dump (route-delta-20270607.txt). We suspect either a NAT translation collapse or selective blackhole during retransmit windows. Can you confirm whether you saw any NAT/PTABLE churn on your side or security group denies for ephemeral ranges?

We can keep the current routes but will roll back if needed — requesting an urgent sync.

Thanks,
--
OrbitBridge NetOps

From: Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwood.com>

Date: 2027-06-07T10:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: abrupt egress stalls after consolidation

Thanks for the packet + route dump. Opening an internal triage.

Quick asks so we can narrow the blast radius:
- Exact timestamps (UTC) for two example incidents you captured in the pcap.
- Was traffic TCP only? Any UDP/large MTU flows in same window?
- Do you see a spike in conntrack or NAT port reuse on your edge nodes?
- Can you confirm the BGP next-hop change + whether ECMP was removed or altered for those prefixes?

Marissa / Karthik / Neha — can you look at the attached pcap and route diff and flag anything obvious (esp. MTU/DF/fragmentation or SNAT churn)? If this looks like a conntrack/NAT collapse we'll need to coordinate a temporary rule to clamp MTU or expand ephemeral ports combined with a scheduled rollback of the consolidation.

I can be on a quick call now if helpful — otherwise please reply here with initial findings.

- Logan
Senior Network Reliability Engineer, Redwood Inference

Logan — timestamps and quick context:
- Incidents at 2027-06-07T01:41:13Z and 2027-06-07T02:22:47Z (two different hosts seen in pcap).
- Mostly TCP (443/80) with some large MTU HTTPS bursts from our caching layer -> upstream APIs.
- Our edge shows conntrack table grows ~30% for ~60s then falls; SNAT translation count briefly drops to zero on the pcap host during the stall period (we captured SYN->SYN-ACK->stall pattern).
- The consolidation removed two ECMP paths in favor of the aggregator next-hop (so fewer distinct outgoing paths).

We have attached the pcap slice + route delta. Happy to share a full trace if you need it.

- OrbitBridge NetOps

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: logan.wright@redwood.com, netops@orbitbridge.com
Cc: karthik.iyer@redwood.com, neha.kapoor@redwood.com
Date: 2027-06-07T12:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: abrupt egress stalls after consolidation

Forwarding quick initial analysis — highlights from the pcap and route dump:

> From the pcap: repeated TCP 3-way handshake attempts where SYNs are retransmitted and intermediate segments show MSS/DF set to 1460. There are many ICMP "Fragmentation needed" messages for flows taking the new aggregator path.

> From route-delta: the aggregator has an MTU of 1500 on our side but we've observed path MTU along the new egress path is 1460 for a subset of upstream hops (likely the transit provider framer).

Two plausible mechanisms:
1) Path MTU mismatch + DF set => blackholed larger segments until endpoints fallback, explaining 30–90s stalls;
2) SNAT translation churn due to rapid ephemeral port reallocation when ECMP was collapsed — in one capture we see the NAT table being flushed by a periodic job (we need to confirm timing of your route change and any SNAT daemon restarts).

Immediate asks for OrbitBridge: can you check whether your hosts set DF on the HTTP stack (kernel/sysctl) and whether any PMTU discovery was disabled? Also, confirm any automation that clears conntrack/NAT tables during topology changes.

I'll run a quick check on our edge SNAT daemon logs and conntrack counters and report back in ~30m. In parallel, Karthik — can you draft an on-the-wire mitigation (MTU clamp on aggregator + temporary conntrack table sizing bump)?

- Marissa
Network Reliability Lead, Redwood Inference

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
To: marissa.cole@redwood.com, logan.wright@redwood.com, netops@orbitbridge.com
Cc: neha.kapoor@redwood.com
Date: 2027-06-07T12:42:00-07:00
Subject: Re: abrupt egress stalls after consolidation

Marissa's summary matches what I see in the logs. Proposed short-term mitigation steps (safe, reversible):
- Apply an MTU clamp of 1460 on the aggregator egress interface (iptables tc/netem if needed) to avoid Path MTU blackholes.
- Increase conntrack_max and net.netfilter.nf_conntrack_tcp_timeout_established temporarily by 2x for 2 hours to avoid aggressive eviction during the churn window.
- Add a transient iptables rule to allow ephemeral port range 32768:61000 explicitly in the AGG egress security group to rule out SG-induced drops.

I'll prepare a one-click rollback and a runbook entry. If OrbitBridge is okay we can apply the MTU clamp during a low-risk window and monitor.

Doc: proposed-remediation-playbook.md attached.

- Karthik
Senior Software Reliability Engineer (Networking), Redwood Inference

From: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: abrupt egress stalls after consolidation

Following up with verification steps and a proposed schedule:

Verification performed overnight (logs from 2027-06-07 23:00–03:00 UTC):
- conntrack_max reached ~89% at 2027-06-07T02:21:40Z on two edge nodes coincident with your stalled flows. No full table drop, but eviction rate spiked.
- Our SNAT service restarted briefly at 2027-06-07T02:21:34Z — that aligns with your observed SNAT translation drop; likely the SNAT health-check restarted due to a transient control-plane event after ECMP removal.

Proposed immediate schedule (coord with OrbitBridge):
1) 2027-06-08T16:00 UTC — Apply MTU clamp 1460 and increase conntrack sizing for 2 hours as a test window.
2) Monitor 30m for packet retransmit reduction and conntrack eviction stats; rollback if any unexpected failures.
3) If stable, plan a follow-up config change: avoid SNAT daemon restarts during peering changes (change health-check hooks) and document MTU on aggregator path.

OrbitBridge: please confirm you can be available at 16:00 UTC and if you prefer we do a controlled rollback instead of the MTU clamp.

- Neha
Networks Ops, Redwood Inference
